meta.name: wall-bracket
meta.summary: Shelf bracket: 1.5 kg static load on a 60 mm arm, printed in PETG

params.name: arm_length
params.rationale: mm, wall face to the load point. The design's driving dimension: deflection goes as L^3, so a 25% longer arm is very nearly a doubling. 80 was the first number asked for and it put deflection at 1.7mm — over three times the limit — with no thickness that recovered it inside the print time budget.

params.name: width
params.rationale: mm, across the bracket. Stiffness is linear in width and cubic in thickness, so widening is the expensive way to buy stiffness and thickening is the cheap one — but see `thickness`, which has its own ceiling.

params.name: thickness
params.rationale: mm, and DELIBERATELY still failing the deflection claim in this reference project — it comes out at ~0.70mm against a 0.5mm limit. 8.0 passes at 0.47mm. The default is left marginal so `atompipe check` on a fresh clone shows a real gate catching a real problem, and so the fix is one parameter you can watch turn green. Deflection goes as 1/t^3, which is why thickness is the cheap lever; 4.0 was tried and misses by ~5x.

params.name: hole_d
params.rationale: mm, clearance for an M5 fastener. M5 free-fit is 5.5; 5.0 would be a line-to-line fit that an FDM hole will not hold to.

params.name: n_bolts
params.rationale: Two bolts, not one: a single fastener lets the bracket rotate about it under an off-centre load, and nothing in this model would catch that.

params.name: edge_margin
params.rationale: mm, from the hole EDGE to the nearest free edge (not the hole centre — the distinction is worth stating because getting it wrong silently halves your tear-out margin). The usual minimum against tear-out is one hole diameter of material beyond the hole, and 8.0 against a 5.5mm hole is comfortably past it.

params.name: load_n
params.rationale: N at the arm tip, static. ~1.5 kg. Declared static: this model has no fatigue or impact term, and a claim that says otherwise would be lying.

params.name: safety_factor
params.rationale: Design stress is yield / safety_factor. 2.0 is the conventional floor for a static, non-life-safety load in a ductile material. An FDM part arguably wants 3.0; the example keeps 2.0 so the default configuration is interesting rather than trivially over-built.

params.name: material
params.rationale: Key into MATERIALS. PETG over PLA because this part lives on a wall and PLA creeps under sustained load at room temperature — a PLA bracket that passes every gate here will still sag over months, and nothing in a static analysis sees that. Swap to alu6061 and the deflection claim passes by a wide margin at triple the mass.

params.name: nozzle_d
params.rationale: mm. Sets the minimum printable wall (see derived `min_wall`).

params.name: bed_xy
params.rationale: mm, printer bed. The usable figure is smaller — see `usable_bed` below.

params.name: brim_mm
params.rationale: mm of brim allowance per side. A part sized to the raw bed does not fit a bed once the brim is on it, which is the kind of thing you discover at 11pm.
